title: Portal Window: Workspace Gateway & Micro-rail Navigation System
creator: Priya Narang
description: Design and prototype a new compact workspace gateway that sits in the left rail and acts as a lightweight ‘portal window’ into another workspace. Primary goals: reduce context-switch friction, surface per-workspace cost and latency lenses, and simplify keyboard-first switching for power users. Deliverables: high-fidelity prototype, accessible interaction spec, annotated handoff to frontend, and experiment plan for incremental rollout.

design_decisions: Persistent micro-rail over transient tooltip: supports quick comparisons between two workspaces without repeated clicks.
Use cached snapshot with infrequent refresh for preview content to avoid high backend load; provide manual refresh action in preview header.
Show per-workspace cost chips (24h spend + sparkline) as primary signal inside switcher to help triage cost regressions quickly.
Compact layout prioritizes left-rail real estate: avatar-sized workspace token, short title, cost chip, last activity time, overflow menu for workspace actions.
Keyboard-first access: prefix hotkey (Cmd/Ctrl+K) to open switcher, arrow navigation, Enter to open workspace, Space to expand portal preview.
Accessibility: preview must be reachable via keyboard, expose title and role to screen readers, color contrast and motion reduced mode supported.
Deferred items for MVP: drag-and-drop reordering, inline rollout controls, and interactive charts inside preview (phase 2).
accept_criteria: Design assets and tokens committed to the design system (icons, chip styles, micro-rail spacing).
High-fidelity prototype with desktop and keyboard interactions documented.
Annotated behavior spec covering focus management, refresh cadence, and failure states.
Accessibility checklist met (ARIA roles, contrast, keyboard traps documented).
Handoff package in Confluence with engineering tasks broken out and dependencies called out (ENG-2218, ENG-2280).
usability_findings: Internal round 1 (n=6): Users preferred persistent preview for comparison tasks; initial confusion about what data is live vs snapshot — resolved by explicit 'snapshot' label and refresh button.
Participants asked for cost signal granularity — aggregated 24h spend plus sparkline was adequate for initial discovery workflows.
Power users requested keyboard shortcuts and quick-open behavior; added to acceptance criteria.
Some participants worried about leaking sensitive info in previews across workspaces; added permission gating and filtering to scope previews to metadata-only view for non-admins.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal beta (10% of employees) — gather qualitative feedback and bug reports.
Phase 1: Canary (5% of customers, non-critical accounts) — monitor switch success rate and latency for 72 hours.
Phase 2: Gradual ramp (25% -> 50% -> 100%) over 2 weeks with automated rollback on defined SLO breaches.
Experimentation: A/B test with control (current switcher) vs variant (portal window) on task completion time for cross-workspace comparisons.
Telemetry: ensure ENG-2280 captures switch latency, preview refresh rate, user toggles, and cost-lens engagement.
metrics: Workspace switch time (ms) — median and 95th percentile.
Preview open rate (percent of switches that expand preview).
Cost-lens engagement (clicks on cost chip -> cost dashboard).
Time-to-task for cross-workspace comparison tasks (measured via A/B test).
Error rate for preview renders and refresh failures.
next_steps: Finalize accessibility spec and hand off to ENG-2218 for left-rail integration.
Coordinate with Analytics to implement telemetry events (ENG-2280) before canary rollout.
Run a 10-person internal beta week (dates: 2026-03-21 to 2026-03-27) and collect session recordings.
Prep marketing/internal launch notes and a short walkthrough video for Solutions Engineering.
Schedule follow-up design critique after internal beta to decide phase 2 feature set (drag-to-reorder, inline rollouts).
